# Private N16 concurrent accepted-work control

The same framework-dependent AppSurface deployment supplies the privileged C#
supervisor and its nonroot worker. The compile-owned `EvidencePrivateQualification=N16`
image sends a fixed authenticated workload request, retains it while its accepted
body is blocked, and uses separate authenticated STOP and WAIT requests to join
that body. Ordinary builds retain `None` and cannot invoke this private control.

## Invocation and ownership

The workflow builds the pinned source and dependency graph with SDK 10.0.401,
then copies the framework-dependent payload and runtime 10.0.12 into protected
root-owned directories. `run-native.py` drives the fixed acquisition, source/ELF
inspection, root fixture and private retention sequence under original cumulative
deadlines. It supplies no caller-selected operation, process argument, admission
callback or producer registration. The root fixture observes the actual original
root process terminal, generated worker/owner units and cgroups, output bytes,
workspace, and named/reverse account deletion. Failure quarantines the owned paths.

The five stderr frames contain accepted-work data, kernel output data, the
original fixed failure, a final cleanup record, and the unchanged full ASEVD410
message. The actual Unix root exit remains 1. Parser success is diagnostic data;
original process settlement, immutable source/build/runtime/OS bindings, complete
EOF/quota checks and final root custody must also hold. No native result opens
Trusted eligibility or the production catalogue.

## Failure-only client progress

The private C# worker writes fixed ordered `ASEVDN16C:01` through `:06`, `ASEVDN16X:01` through `:05`, then `ASEVDN16C:07` lines to its existing stderr stream at the original request, control, response and EXIT milestones. The complete controlled sequence is checked byte-for-byte before its unchanged fixed rejection line. The [record parser](check_n16_records.py) requires the exact combined stream and digest, both original EOFs and
all existing kernel, accepted-work and cleanup checks.

The separate `issue779-n16-progress-diagnostic-v2` record is failure-only and is emitted only when
accepted-work projection has not been attempted. Its 21 closed fields include
`client_last_milestone`, `client_joined_stream_complete`,
`client_marker_sequence_valid`, `client_exit_stage`, `client_exit_failure_class` and
`client_exit_diagnostic_code`, with no authority or acceptance. The C# root
reads markers only from the original joined output receipt. This earlier failure
record is retained privately for diagnosis; it cannot replace the complete four
JSON records and terminal message required to qualify this control. A completed
accepted-work projection intentionally has no extra progress JSON record.

## Retained evidence

`retain-native.sh` selects fixed N16 paths only, preserves root-only regular
single-link files through identity and digest checks, and emits bounded canonical
USTAR. Root stdout must be empty; stderr is limited to 114688 bytes. Summary and
fixture-result records are limited to 4096 bytes, the request to 65536 bytes, and
the two full-path request/policy checksum rows to 4096 bytes. Both rows must bind
the exact retained request and the fixed fixture policy, in their original order.
The existing 32 MiB aggregate bound and cumulative
30-second retention deadline remain unchanged. Raw bytes are never public output.

The [runner](run-native.py) attempts [retention](retain-native.sh) after every
fixture dispatch outcome. Diagnostic collection cannot replace the original
failed outcome. Receipt publication also fails closed when writing, printing or
the original deadline fails; a successful fixture without a published receipt
cannot return success.

## Preparation paths and API contracts

The root bootstrap retains the reviewed [acquisition script](acquire-inbound.sh),
[transport script](prepare-root-inputs-v2.sh), fixture and parser plus the source
capture before privileged interpretation. The source capture has its own 2 MiB
bound; ordinary reviewed scripts retain the 128 KiB bound. Acquisition reads the
fixed `capture-receipt.json` directly from that protected bootstrap directory.

Acquisition creates the root-owned inbound tree. Transport accepts
`--source-commit` and copies its control records and scripts into a separate
protected input tree. The runner supplies every option exactly once. The
unprivileged [OS dependency audit](prepare-os-audit-v2.py) and the root
[fixture](checkpoint-n16-accepted-work.sh) use the transported input tree, with
root-only control data and sealed deployment directories. A fixed, empty,
root-owned `empty-audit-helper` directory satisfies the existing audit inventory
API. It contains no helper image, executable or workload.

The build receipt distinguishes the captured source's parent from the installed
harness's parent: the harness is a direct child of the captured source. The
runner and root scripts must preserve that distinction when comparing their
receipts. The fixture observation's five NSS checks are an integer count, not a
boolean. Its root projection is the actual build receipt digest. The detached
[record parser](check_n16_records.py) is interpreted only from retained bytes
whose digest matches the reviewed parser.

## Pruned cgroup record correction

The v11 Linux records reached accepted work, body join, STOP, WAIT and EXIT commits, with the fixed 257-byte worker stderr and all original joins. The data parser rejected the observed kernel-pruned group because it required event booleans and inode numbers even when the group no longer existed. This packet accepts the two exact kernel shapes: a present group with false populated/frozen events and valid inode identity, or an absent group with all subordinate fields null. Present unknown facts and invented absent-group facts reject. Original process, unit, NSS, output, custody, deadline and launch-join checks remain mandatory. The record correction is not native qualification; a complete fresh fixture run is still required.

## Exit diagnostic preparation correction

This input revision uses captured source `a6933fa3dc2c7a88832abf337447f88527477703`
with direct source parent `0adef6032217b4181898a4d6d129e1248cb0eda3`.
The harness parent is the captured source; the source parent is distinct.
The [optional progress parser](check_n16_records.py) requires actual Boolean
values for every progress flag, including `exit_committed`. Both Boolean values
are valid diagnostic data; integer, null, string and container substitutes fail.
This snapshot and the refreshed complete digest chain await independent review.
Local parser tests, source review and build receipts do not prove Linux execution.
The production catalogue, admission, caps and stop/join contracts are unchanged.

### N16 terminal unit retirement

The expected negative worker and root exit one. After the original launch, retained protocol/UID/GID/pump/join records and NSS absence pass, the fixture requires physical generated cgroup absence. It permits only a loaded failed/failed or inactive/dead unit with zero main/control PIDs, no job and an empty or exact generated ControlGroup. It then calls reset-failed on the exact generated unit and requires not-found within the original fixture deadline. Pre-run not-found checks remain strict. Resetting metadata proves no exit, cleanup, custody, admission or acceptance. See [systemd 255 reset-failed](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v255/man/systemctl.xml#L687-L691).

`867aec31f950052666275268f08fe1a7f7fa3c25`, and 2,869 source paths. Its exact capture is

The builder, acquisition, root transport, runner and checkpoint use this same
capture and canonical full SHA/mode projection; raw-file and projection hashes

The failed non-admission case intentionally retains the generation workspace.
After actual worker/owner/handler/pump/launch joins, account deletion and exact
generated-unit retirement, the fixture audits the retained tree through
no-follow directory handles. It requires root-owned 0700 directories, only

0600 single-link control socket, and the root-owned 0400 single-link bounded

The archive consumer validates this same v2 shape, never the old absent-workspace
claim. Original failure, deadline, process/group joins and raw evidence checks
remain mandatory. See the supplied retained-custody independent review.

All installation and publisher review gates remain false/pending until a fresh
review binds these exact composed bytes. Source preparation and data controls
grant no Linux execution credit, native acceptance or Trusted qualification.

## Exact wrapper audit-output correction

The previous outer archive consumer rejected a dispatched N16 fixture because
its twelve full-tree audit rows preceded the fixed terminal marker. The new
consumer derives the exact ordered rows from the independently validated
same-host source/tool/runtime maps. The sealed tool row adds exactly one
canonical fixture-policy file: one additional node and its actual byte length;
the file-row column remains the count of the original manifest-bound inputs.
Missing, reordered, additional, altered or malformed rows reject. Every existing
record-parser, source, request, OS identity, EOF, quota, account and retained
workspace check remains required. This correction adds no product code or runtime
authority. Review and publication gates remain pending.

The previous watcher bootstrap-token diagnosis was unsupported: the token was
echoed workflow source, while retained command receipts show successful bootstrap
and actual C# dispatch. The immutable failed runner receipt remains exit one.
The retained four-record native contract must be independently revalidated before
any control credit; a wrapper regression alone is not a new Linux execution.
